top_story: Israel’s 20 August admission that its troops fired on the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab and six relatives were killed, alongside Itamar Ben-Gvir’s public promotion of gallows for Palestinians tried in military courts, sharpened the sense that accountability remains selective and that punitive symbolism is being normalized inside Israeli politics. Those moves deepen Palestinian distrust at a moment when the human toll of the war already shapes daily life in Gaza far more than any legal process announced after the fact. Four days later, Washington removed Syria from its state sponsors of terrorism list, opening a path for investment and signaling a broader shift from isolation toward managed reengagement with Damascus as reconstruction pressures mount. Together, these developments point to a regional landscape in which outside powers are recalibrating political relationships while civilians still face the consequences of entrenched impunity and uneven recovery.
